Sentence (English): Its large capacity makes it convenient to use.
Comments (English): Honestly, I understand why people say that once you start using a dishwasher, it's hard to go back to handwashing. The LG Dios Objet Collection 14-seater built-in dishwasher I recently installed is a product I'm extremely satisfied with, from its design to its performance. First of all, the Objet Collection Nature Beige color is absolutely beautiful. It's understated yet luxurious, and it blends seamlessly with my kitchen interior. Its built-in design makes the entire kitchen feel much more organized. It's an appliance, but it feels like furniture, and I'm always satisfied with it. When it comes to performance, LG is unwavering. The 100C True Steam function ensures reliable sterilization. It claims to eliminate 99.999% of harmful bacteria, so I can use it with confidence, even on children's dishes or other dishes I'm concerned about hygiene. Even greasy dishes and stuck-on food come out clean after washing, leaving the dishwasher feeling much cleaner than when I wash by hand. I especially love the Tornado cleaning blade. The powerful water jets from all directions ensure even cleaning without having to worry about the position of the dishes. Even heavily greased dishes like frying pans and pots are cleaned in one go. The large capacity for 14 people means I only need to do it once a day. Since it can hold dishes, cups, and pots all at once, the stress of piling up dishes is greatly reduced. The well-organized interior makes organizing dishes a breeze, and the capacity is perfect for a family. I'm also very satisfied with the drying function. Thanks to the automatic door opening, the door opens slightly after the wash is finished, allowing the dishes to dry naturally. This virtually eliminates water stains and quickly removes moisture from the interior. It's incredibly convenient because it automatically does the job without having to keep the door open. Another great feature is the UP feature. I was amazed by how the features update while I was using it, and the fact that it maintains the latest features over time is highly satisfying. It's not just a great appliance for the moment, but also a product I'll want to keep for a long time. It's also a top-rated energy-efficient product, which reduces electricity bills. And with a single wash using only 14.5 liters of water, it's significantly more economical than washing dishes by hand. Weighing 43kg, it's been stable and comfortable since its built-in installation. Overall, I'm very satisfied with the design and interior design. Its powerful cleaning and sterilizing power are excellent. Its large capacity makes it convenient to use. It even has automatic drying and smart features. It's a well-equipped product, so I can definitely recommend it to anyone considering a dishwasher. My time in the kitchen has become much more comfortable, and the stress of washing dishes has disappeared, significantly improving my quality of life. Since installing it, I'm so satisfied that I wonder why I didn't get it sooner.

Sentence (English): It's a well-equipped product, so I can definitely recommend it to anyone considering a dishwasher.
Comments (English): Honestly, I understand why people say that once you start using a dishwasher, it's hard to go back to handwashing. The LG Dios Objet Collection 14-seater built-in dishwasher I recently installed is a product I'm extremely satisfied with, from its design to its performance. First of all, the Objet Collection Nature Beige color is absolutely beautiful. It's understated yet luxurious, and it blends seamlessly with my kitchen interior. Its built-in design makes the entire kitchen feel much more organized. It's an appliance, but it feels like furniture, and I'm always satisfied with it. When it comes to performance, LG is unwavering. The 100C True Steam function ensures reliable sterilization. It claims to eliminate 99.999% of harmful bacteria, so I can use it with confidence, even on children's dishes or other dishes I'm concerned about hygiene. Even greasy dishes and stuck-on food come out clean after washing, leaving the dishwasher feeling much cleaner than when I wash by hand. I especially love the Tornado cleaning blade. The powerful water jets from all directions ensure even cleaning without having to worry about the position of the dishes. Even heavily greased dishes like frying pans and pots are cleaned in one go. The large capacity for 14 people means I only need to do it once a day. Since it can hold dishes, cups, and pots all at once, the stress of piling up dishes is greatly reduced. The well-organized interior makes organizing dishes a breeze, and the capacity is perfect for a family. I'm also very satisfied with the drying function. Thanks to the automatic door opening, the door opens slightly after the wash is finished, allowing the dishes to dry naturally. This virtually eliminates water stains and quickly removes moisture from the interior. It's incredibly convenient because it automatically does the job without having to keep the door open. Another great feature is the UP feature. I was amazed by how the features update while I was using it, and the fact that it maintains the latest features over time is highly satisfying. It's not just a great appliance for the moment, but also a product I'll want to keep for a long time. It's also a top-rated energy-efficient product, which reduces electricity bills. And with a single wash using only 14.5 liters of water, it's significantly more economical than washing dishes by hand. Weighing 43kg, it's been stable and comfortable since its built-in installation. Overall, I'm very satisfied with the design and interior design. Its powerful cleaning and sterilizing power are excellent. Its large capacity makes it convenient to use. It even has automatic drying and smart features. It's a well-equipped product, so I can definitely recommend it to anyone considering a dishwasher. My time in the kitchen has become much more comfortable, and the stress of washing dishes has disappeared, significantly improving my quality of life. Since installing it, I'm so satisfied that I wonder why I didn't get it sooner.

I'll never understand why these companies don't turn the bottom rack, when you stack plates in, and close it, the plates roll out of the spacers. Also, with the 3rd rack, they could have eliminated the silverware tray on the bottom, added more dividers, and had more room for large items. It is a good quality dishwasher but I wish I would have known about these things and possibly looked at other brands.

Sentence (English): This is a review of a dishwasher I bought with my own money.
Comments (English): [ I am satisfied with the cost-effectiveness, cleaning power, and design. ] || ---------------- || This is a review of a dishwasher I bought with my own money. I bought this after getting stressed out from throwing away my small dishwasher and having to handwash dishes. I've used single- and double-sized dishwashers before when I lived in a studio apartment, but they were quite inconvenient. Because they were so small, pots and pans barely fit, and the manual pouring of water was a hassle. Ultimately, I got rid of it when I moved and went back to handwashing. Either way, the hassle was similar, so I don't regret throwing it away. But since I work overtime often and eat dinner at home, the daily dishwashing became a huge burden. It was okay on days when I just reheated a meal, but if I made even a stew, I had to do the dishes twice—once while I was cooking and once afterward. It made the whole day, which should have been spent enjoying a nice meal and relaxing, feel incredibly difficult. So, I started considering a dishwasher again, and this time, I decided against buying anything small. The drawbacks I'd experienced before were so obvious that I didn't want to make the same choice again. My job isn't stable, so I move quite often. I still disliked the drain connection, but I hated having to pour water into it even more. Ultimately, I decided to accept the plumbing connection, but upgrade the size to fit a 5-6 person dishwasher, enough to accommodate a pot or two. I compared several products, but I was looking for something cost-effective rather than overly expensive, and I chose this one. The clean white design makes it easy to place anywhere in the kitchen without standing out. The size is impressive, befitting a 6-person dishwasher, but it's not overly clunky, and the overall finish is surprisingly good. The automatic door opening feature helps remove moisture from the interior after drying, which is much better than nothing. However, even with the hot air dryer on, there's still quite a bit of moisture after the dishwasher is finished. The interior is definitely spacious, so I can fit plates, bowls, cups, and even a pot or two, if I play Tetris. This alone makes me much more satisfied with this dishwasher than my previous small one. The operating time is definitely on the long side. I knew this before purchasing it, and it actually is. Maybe it's because I've only used small ones? It was only 30 minutes on high speed. I understand if it's because of the size. So I mostly use it on the shortest low-temperature mode. Still, it cleans most of my daily dishes well, so I have no major complaints. There's some noise, but it's not so loud that I find it annoying. If you're concerned about it, it bothers you, and if you're not, it doesn't bother you. So, even running it at night didn't significantly disrupt my daily routine. Oh, but it was a bit bothersome when I was sleeping. When dishwashers first became widespread, I honestly thought machines couldn't keep up with hand-washing. Now, I don't think machines can keep up with the menial tasks I do by hand. In short, I recommend this to anyone who, like me, cooks frequently at home but finds dishwashing stressful. Either way, the hassle was similar, so I don't regret throwing it away. But since I work overtime often and eat dinner at home, the daily dishwashing became a huge burden. It was okay on days when I just reheated a meal, but if I made even a stew, I had to do the dishes twice—once while I was cooking and once afterward. It made the whole day, which should have been spent enjoying a nice meal and relaxing, feel incredibly difficult. So, I started considering a dishwasher again, and this time, I decided against buying anything small. The drawbacks I'd experienced before were so obvious that I didn't want to make the same choice again. My job isn't stable, so I move quite often. I still disliked the drain connection, but I hated having to pour water into it even more. Ultimately, I decided to accept the plumbing connection, but upgrade the size to fit a 5-6 person dishwasher, enough to accommodate a pot or two. I compared several products, but I was looking for something cost-effective rather than overly expensive, and I chose this one. The clean white design makes it easy to place anywhere in the kitchen without standing out. The size is impressive, befitting a 6-person dishwasher, but it's not overly clunky, and the overall finish is surprisingly good. The automatic door opening feature helps remove moisture from the interior after drying, which is much better than nothing. However, even with the hot air dryer on, there's still quite a bit of moisture after the dishwasher is finished. The interior is definitely spacious, so I can fit plates, bowls, cups, and even a pot or two, if I play Tetris. This alone makes me much more satisfied with this dishwasher than my previous small one. The operating time is definitely on the long side. I knew this before purchasing it, and it actually is. Maybe it's because I've only used small ones? It was only 30 minutes on high speed. I understand if it's because of the size. So I mostly use it on the shortest low-temperature mode. Still, it cleans most of my daily dishes well, so I have no major complaints. There's some noise, but it's not so loud that I find it annoying. If you're concerned about it, it bothers you, and if you're not, it doesn't bother you. So, even running it at night didn't significantly disrupt my daily routine. Oh, but it was a bit bothersome when I was sleeping. When dishwashers first became widespread, I honestly thought machines couldn't keep up with hand-washing. Now, I don't think machines can keep up with the menial tasks I do by hand. In short, I recommend this to anyone who, like me, cooks frequently at home but finds dishwashing stressful. I think anyone who's ever been disappointed with a small dishwasher will be even more satisfied. Those who want a perfectly quiet and fast product may be disappointed, but considering the cost-effectiveness and practicality, it is satisfactory.

I still disliked the drain connection, but I hated having to pour water into it even more. Ultimately, I decided to accept the plumbing connection, but upgrade the size to fit a 5-6 person dishwasher, enough to accommodate a pot or two. Those who want a perfectly quiet and fast product may be disappointed, but considering the cost-effectiveness and practicality, it is satisfactory.

Sentence (English): This unit was advertised as having fold-down tines on both the upper and lower racks per Lowe's website.
Comments (English): [ Not as advertised ] || ---------------- || This unit was advertised as having fold-down tines on both the upper and lower racks per Lowe's website. I also confirmed this was true by checking out the model display at my local Lowe's. The unit that was shipped to me has ZERO folding tines on the lower rack and 1 row of folding tines on the upper rack. This is quite disappointing as I chose this model because I wanted the flexibility. The tines on the bottom rack do not even hold plates fully upright which I don't understand. I have no complaints about the washing or drying abilities as of yet, but do agree that the normal cycle with heated dry is about twice as long as it needs to be. I also find the normal cycle to be more quiet than the quick wash. While the dishwasher does look very nice, it also feels cheap, particularly with the door. I can push the stainless cover in with just the pressure of my finger, and I think this is partially why the dishwasher is louder than I was expecting.

Sentence (English): It's a dishwasher that cleans like a dream and is completely silent, but what I love most is that it only opens the door when it's finished, so the containers don't come out soaking wet.
Comments (English): [ It's not just a dishwasher, it's real convenience. ] || ---------------- || It's a dishwasher that cleans like a dream and is completely silent, but what I love most is that it only opens the door when it's finished, so the containers don't come out soaking wet. The third rack on top is a total win because it frees up so much space below for pots and pans, although the Eco program takes forever if you're in a hurry. The only downside is that the inner base is plastic and not stainless steel, but considering how well it cleans and how little energy it uses, it more than makes up for it. Plus, the notification on your phone when it's done is a huge plus so you don't have to keep checking on it.
Comments (Original): [ No es solo un lavavajillas, es comodidad real ] || ---------------- || Es un lavavajillas que lava de cine y no hace nada de ruido, pero lo que más me gusta es que abre la puerta solo al terminar y así los tuppers no salen empapados. La tercera bandeja de arriba es un acierto total porque ganas mucho sitio abajo para las ollas, aunque el programa Eco se hace eterno si tienes prisa. La única pega es que la base interior es de plástico y no de acero, pero por lo bien que limpia y lo poco que gasta, compensa de sobra. Además, que te avise al móvil cuando acaba es un puntazo para no estar pendiente.

Sentence (English): This is a review of a dishwasher I bought with my own money.
Comments (English): [ I am satisfied with the cost-effectiveness, cleaning power, and design. ] || ---------------- || This is a review of a dishwasher I bought with my own money. I bought this after getting stressed out from throwing away my small dishwasher and having to handwash dishes. I've used single- and double-sized dishwashers before when I lived in a studio apartment, but they were quite inconvenient. Because they were so small, pots and pans barely fit, and the manual pouring of water was a hassle. Ultimately, I got rid of it when I moved and went back to handwashing. Either way, the hassle was similar, so I don't regret throwing it away. But since I work overtime often and eat dinner at home, the daily dishwashing became a huge burden. It was okay on days when I just reheated a meal, but if I made even a stew, I had to do the dishes twice—once while I was cooking and once afterward. It made the whole day, which should have been spent enjoying a nice meal and relaxing, feel incredibly difficult. So, I started considering a dishwasher again, and this time, I decided against buying anything small. The drawbacks I'd experienced before were so obvious that I didn't want to make the same choice again. My job isn't stable, so I move quite often. I still disliked the drain connection, but I hated having to pour water into it even more. Ultimately, I decided to accept the plumbing connection, but upgrade the size to fit a 5-6 person dishwasher, enough to accommodate a pot or two. I compared several products, but I was looking for something cost-effective rather than overly expensive, and I chose this one. The clean white design makes it easy to place anywhere in the kitchen without standing out. The size is impressive, befitting a 6-person dishwasher, but it's not overly clunky, and the overall finish is surprisingly good. The automatic door opening feature helps remove moisture from the interior after drying, which is much better than nothing. However, even with the hot air dryer on, there's still quite a bit of moisture after the dishwasher is finished. The interior is definitely spacious, so I can fit plates, bowls, cups, and even a pot or two, if I play Tetris. This alone makes me much more satisfied with this dishwasher than my previous small one. The operating time is definitely on the long side. I knew this before purchasing it, and it actually is. Maybe it's because I've only used small ones? It was only 30 minutes on high speed. I understand if it's because of the size. So I mostly use it on the shortest low-temperature mode. Still, it cleans most of my daily dishes well, so I have no major complaints. There's some noise, but it's not so loud that I find it annoying. If you're concerned about it, it bothers you, and if you're not, it doesn't bother you. So, even running it at night didn't significantly disrupt my daily routine. Oh, but it was a bit bothersome when I was sleeping. When dishwashers first became widespread, I honestly thought machines couldn't keep up with hand-washing. Now, I don't think machines can keep up with the menial tasks I do by hand. In short, I recommend this to anyone who, like me, cooks frequently at home but finds dishwashing stressful. I think anyone who's ever been disappointed with a small dishwasher will be even more satisfied. Those who want a perfectly quiet and fast product may be disappointed, but considering the cost-effectiveness and actual use, I am satisfied~. . (Additional one-month review) The electricity bill increased by about 16,000 won. I used it once a day on weekdays and once or twice on weekends.

So, I started considering a dishwasher again, and this time, I decided against buying anything small. The drawbacks I'd experienced before were so obvious that I didn't want to make the same choice again. My job isn't stable, so I move quite often. I still disliked the drain connection, but I hated having to pour water into it even more. Ultimately, I decided to accept the plumbing connection, but upgrade the size to fit a 5-6 person dishwasher, enough to accommodate a pot or two. I compared several products, but I was looking for something cost-effective rather than overly expensive, and I chose this one. The automatic door opening feature helps remove moisture from the interior after drying, which is much better than nothing. Now, I don't think machines can keep up with the menial tasks I do by hand. In short, I recommend this to anyone who, like me, cooks frequently at home but finds dishwashing stressful. I think anyone who's ever been disappointed with a small dishwasher will be even more satisfied. Those who want a perfectly quiet and fast product may be disappointed, but considering the cost-effectiveness and actual use, I am satisfied~. . Comments (English): [ I really dislike this machine ] || ---------------- || I do not like this machine at all. I would give it zero stars if the format would allow. So 1 star for being quiet. It is very quiet, and I have no complaint on its cleaning ability. Although it does take a long time to wash. My old machine did not take as long.I really dislike the rack designs and the fact that it doesn't have a dry cycle like my old one. If you like to towel dry your dishes or constantly be on alert to open the door to let them air dry while it is still hot, then you might be happy with this machine. Also the bottom rack does not easily roll out onto the open door. It seems to always jump its track, or something impedes the smooth operation. Perhaps its just my particular utensil set and tine spacing that my forks seem to fall through the basket and stop the bottom rack from sliding out. Yes, I could learn to keep the forks pointing upward to prevent that, but I am of the mindset that pointy things should point down in order to prevent accidental injuries to hands. I do not care for the stainless steel door because it shows all the fingerprints. I hate the design of the retractable hose and power cord for 2 reasons. 1) is that it's not centered on the machine and requires the machine to be offset in front of the sink in order to reach the electric receptacle. This makes my small kitchen space even less usable when the dishwasher is in use. 2) is the quality and care put into the manufacture. It is awkward and twisted and does not easily pull out or retract, or even stay in the recess that is there to store the faucet connection.I really wanted to like this machine, but I cannot wait to replace it.

Comments (English): [ Excellent Dishwasher ] || ---------------- || Old dishwasher needing replacing when the drying fan failed and require practically a full disassembly to replace a simple fan. Red flashing floor light signals a problem, usually forgot to press start button. 3) Tried a messy casserole dish in lower rack and it got it fully cleaned. The bad: 1) Rinse aid is practically required for dry dishes. 2) Should have a blue floor light to signal clean dishes. 3) The phone app is essentially required for: a) knowing when dishes are clean. b) knowing when rinse aid is low.

Sentence (English): Washing dishes used to be the most tedious chore, but this product has definitely made life easier.
Comments (English): Washing dishes used to be the most tedious chore, but this product has definitely made life easier. First of all, I liked the countertop design, making it easy to install. Simply place it on the sink, connect the water supply and drain, and it's ready to use, eliminating the need for any additional construction. It also doesn't take up much kitchen space, making it ideal for single- or two-person households. The cleaning power exceeded my expectations. Even using the standard cycle, grease and food residue from dishes and bowls are thoroughly removed. Even dishes with kimchi soup or greasy frying pans come out clean, which is satisfying. The high-temperature wash also feels hygienic, giving me peace of mind. The auto-open feature after washing helps remove moisture from the inside. However, because it uses a blower dryer, some moisture may remain on plastic cups or concave dishes. Personally, I didn't find it too inconvenient; letting it air-dry for a while or wiping it down with a dry cloth was sufficient. The noise level is surprisingly low, making it comfortable to use in the evenings and nights. The simple button controls also make it easy to adapt, even for those unfamiliar with machines. The coffee cup holder broke after applying too much force. I considered getting it repaired, but it seems more convenient without it, so I'm going to just keep using it. Overall Review: This dishwasher definitely reduces dishwashing time and adds a bit of space to your daily routine. Sentence (English): I've had the dishwasher for a month now.
Comments (English): [ Cleans well but could be more adjustable ] || ---------------- || I've had the dishwasher for a month now. It replaced an LG that I loved but wasn't reliable. I took the advice to go back to Bosch. Overall it's a very good dishwasher, the dishes come out clean and even in the most efficient drying mode are reasonably dry. The app is great, allowing a specific delay time. However, notice that opening it during the delay means start needs to be pressed again (more on that later). There are two issues that could be improved: 1. During operation you can see it's running with a light. Initially I turned that off because it is a red light on the floor but since it's the only indication outside of the app, I turned it back on. But that turns off when it finishes and the door automatically opens. My son twice put dirty dishes in, there needs to be a way to show it's clean and an external sign is a workaround not a solution. In the same vein when it's on a delayed start there's no way to see that, again my son opened it to put something in and the cycle was cancelled. 2. It's not just adjustable enough. I knew that buying it, but there wasn't anything better so I sucked it up. The top shelves adjust up and down ok but there is only one section on the bottom where the tines go down partially. It should allow areas on the top and bottom rack to have no tines. Big items are hard to go in.

Sentence (English): I got a new kitchen installed (white) and thought it was a good time to also replace all my appliances.
Comments (English): [ Quiet and elegant worker in my white kitchen ] || ---------------- || I got a new kitchen installed (white) and thought it was a good time to also replace all my appliances. I already had an ASKO dishwasher and was happy with it. The only issue I had with it was a leaking hose after 7 years. I was able to sell the old washer ($250 not bad I thought! ) and got this sparkling new white one to blend in with my white kitchen. I didn't want an integrated machine, but wanted the look. It looks great (and the white is even cheaper than the silver one) and more importantly works like a dream. I love how there's no branding or buttons visible from the front. Where this is different from my previous machine is that it's much quieter and more electronic whizz bang. It is so quiet I can't always tell if its on, so have to check the light at the bottom! I really like the interior light and the open door feature at the end of a cycle. I wasn't initially too keen on the utensil shelf as I think it's too finicky to load and unload all the utensils from a tray, but it has grown on my as I use it for large utensils and still do the majority of my utensils in the basket. Yes the ASKO is more expensive than some other brands, but if you value quiet, reliabililty and aesthetics, this is the one for you.

Sentence (English): I'm moving and buying a dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ <내돈내산> ] || ---------------- || I'm moving and buying a dishwasher. I was curious because everyone praised it as much as the dryer. Hahahahahahahahaha^^. Why did I buy it now? Of course, I couldn't buy it in my previous house because there wasn't enough space to put it. I bought it because my house is a little bigger. If you have a built-in sink, you have to plan the cabinets and install it. When you move, you have to restore it to its original condition, and then plan the cabinets and install it again in the new house. I asked my younger sibling who uses the existing dishwasher, and they were sick of hearing about it;; . I bought a freestanding one because I have the space (over 60cm) so I can just carry it and install it like a water purifier when I move. It can also be built-in if needed. Washing dishes takes about 30 minutes to an hour, but I like that time because I can do other things. I can do 1-2 days' worth at once. But when it comes to choosing a dishwasher, how you play Tetris is the most important thing. I always think about it.

Comments (English): [ <내돈내산> ] || ---------------- || I decided to buy a dishwasher for my move. Everyone raves about it as much as a clothes dryer, so I was curious. Hahaha. However, with a dishwasher, I think how you 'Tetris' the pieces is the most important thing. I agonize over it every time.

The app is great, allowing a specific delay time. However, notice that opening it during the delay means start needs to be pressed again (more on that later). There are two issues that could be improved:. 1. During operation you can see it's running with a light. Initially I turned that off because it is a red light on the floor but since it's the only indication outside of the app, I turned it back on. But that turns off when it finishes and the door automatically opens. My son twice put dirty dishes in, there needs to be a way to show it's clean and an external sign is a workaround not a solution. In the same vein when it's on a delayed start there's no way to see that, again my son opened it to put something in and the cycle was cancelled. 2. It's not just adjustable enough. I knew that buying it, but there wasn't anything better so I sucked it up. The top shelves adjust up and down ok but there is only one section on the bottom where the tines go down partially. It should allow areas on the top and bottom rack to have no tines. Big items are hard to go in.

Sentence (English): I bought this dishwasher about a month ago.
Comments (English): [ Solid dishwasher ] || ---------------- || I bought this dishwasher about a month ago. It's very quiet and does a great job cleaning the dishes. I've only had a couple of issues that I'm sure will resolve over time. First is cleaning silicone items. My previous dishwasher could do this without issue, but this Maytag dishwasher seems to leave a slimy residue on them despite using the same detergent. I've already tried using rinse aid and running the "PowerBlast" and "High Temp" modes, but it still leaves a film. I've tried others, but haven't found the right combination yet. The other issue is the door doesn't open easily. It isn't hung up or anything, but the springs aren't adjustable on this model so you have to pull it all the way down. It's not hard to do, but compared to other dishwashers I've used it's something you have to adjust to. Since the springs aren't adjustable, this is just how the door is going to be. Overall, I'd recommend this dishwasher. Even with the stainless steel tub, it has some quirks with silicone and door tension, but it cleans dishes much better than previous ones I've used where I'd have to rinse the dishes beforehand. Now I just scrape the solids off, put the dishes in, and it handles the rest. I'd recommend this dishwasher.

Comments (English): [ Authentic review after using it for about 3 weeks ] || ---------------- || First of all, I'm writing this review with a heavy heart, having experienced a significant price drop about a week after purchase and installation. They say knowledge is medicine, but a first-class refund alone won't be enough to convince you otherwise. Buyers should be especially cautious and thrifty when purchasing expensive appliances. Recently, I moved and needed a dishwasher, so I had it installed. Since I was choosing LG appliances, I chose the Dios without hesitation. The installation was also done by an LG technician. It seats 14 people, so it's ample for a three-person household! It has three tiers, with the lowest tier holding plates, large containers, and a frying pan. Of course, to extend the life of the frying pan, I haven't used the dishwasher. The second tier is for cups, rice bowls, and small plates. The height is adjustable, so it's deep enough to accommodate large bowls. The top tier is for utensils like spoons and ladles. This tier is also height-adjustable, so even large ladles can be easily accommodated. The height adjustment is a huge plus. There are two detergent compartments. Liquid or powder detergent goes in the compartment, and solid detergent goes in the bottom basket, which solves the drawbacks of solid detergents. You can adjust the detergent according to the 15/25 markings on the detergent compartment depending on the amount of dishes you're using. I use Natural Pong liquid detergent, and even though I fill all three compartments, I only use up to the 15 mark. Even with that much, dishes with butter or grease are cleaned thoroughly, and there are almost no water stains even without rinse aid. However, the dishwasher's Tetris performance can affect the quality of the dishwashing, so don't stack the dishes too tightly. The Dios dishwasher has a water softener, but the technician told me that it's not necessary in my area (water softeners vary by area), so I don't use it. This product also has a hot air dryer and a 100°C steam wash. After the initial installation, I used the hot air drying function for a while, but now I don't. (The built-in hot air drying function requires annual air filter replacement.) I use it almost exclusively once a day, in the evening. Since the door automatically opens, the clothes are almost completely dry by morning, so I rarely use this function. I might use it occasionally, but I don't think it'll be very often. I've never used the 100°C steam cleaning function. Honestly, I thought both the hot air drying and 100°C steam cleaning functions were essential, so I deliberately chose a product with these features. Personally, I rarely use them. When comparing products, carefully considering your environment and situation will be a great help. Each function can be selected with a light touch. I currently use the automatic cleaning cycle with an additional rinse. The ThinQ app allows you to download multiple cleaning cycles as needed, allowing you to customize them for different situations. Cleaning the interior is conveniently done about once a month, and if you connect it to the ThinQ app, it will notify you when the internal cleaning cycle is due. You don't even need to buy detergent; just add citric acid to the detergent compartment and run the sterilization cycle (in the app). This is a different story, but based on my experience using a different brand of dishwasher, be sure to remove any name stickers attached to water bottles, plates, cutlery, etc., or any product stickers from new products that haven't been removed before putting them in the dishwasher. Stickers can easily get stuck inside the washing blades where the water sprays out. It's amazing how they get there, but you can't remove them yourself; you'll have to hire a technician. I'm very satisfied with everything from installation to use. I replaced my dishwasher after about eight years, and technology has advanced significantly. LG is the best choice for home appliances. If you're considering purchasing a dishwasher, I hope my review was helpful.
Comments (Original): [ 약 3주 사용 찐후기 ] || ---------------- || 우선 구매 및 설치 약 일주일 후부터 현재까지 가격이 대폭 하락해서 속이 많이 쓰린 상태로 작성하는 리뷰입니다.ㅠ알면 병 모르면 약 이라지만..1등급 환급만으로도 정신승리 어렵고ㅠ구매자분들께서는 고가의 가전은 특히 신중+알뜰구매하시길..ㅠ최근 이사하면서 식세기가필요해 로켓설치 받았습니다.가전은 엘지니까 고민없이 디오스로 선택했구요.설치도 엘지 기사님께서 해주셨습니다.14인용이라 3인가구 사용하기에 용량이 넉넉합니다!총 3단으로 최하단은 접시와 큰용기.그리고 후라이팬 적재 가능합니다. 물론 후라이팬 수명연장을 위해 식세기사용은 안하고 있구요ㅎ2단은 컵, 밥공기류와 소접시류 사용하면 되는데요 높낮이 조절이 되니 깊이감이 깊고 큰 그릇도 문제 없습니다.최상단은 숟가락같은 식기류나 국자같은 조리도구용 인데요, 여기도 높이 조절이 되서 큰 국자도 무리없이 적재 됩니다.높이조절이 된다는건 큰 장점 같아요.세제칸은 총 2곳 입니다. 액상이나 가루타입은 세제칸에 넣으면 되고, 고체세제는 최하단 세제바스켓에 넣어주면 되니 고체세제의단점도 해결해주네요.세제는 식기양에 따라 세제칸의 15/25 눈금표시에 맞춰 조절해서 사용하면 되는데 저는 자연퐁 액상세제 사용중이고 식세기 3칸 다채워도 15지점까지만 넣어 사용합니다.그만큼만 사용해도 버터나 고기기름 묻은 그릇도 뽀득하게 세척 잘 되구여 린스사용 안해도 물얼룩 거의 안남습니다.대신 식세기는 테트리스를 어떻게 잘 하느냐에 따라 설거지의 완성도(?)에도 영향이 있으니 그릇 너무 포개서 넣지 마시길.디오스 식세기에는 연수장치도 되어 있는데 기사님께서 저희동네는 연수장치 안써도 된다셔서 (동네마다 다르다 하십니다) 이 기능은 사용 안하고 있어요. 또한 이 제품은 열풍건조에 100도씨 스팀세척까지 가능한 제품인데요첫 설치 후 한동안은 열풍건조기능 쓰다가 지금은 안씁니다.(열풍건조 기능 내장되어있어 에어필터 연1회 교체 필요)거의 하루에 한번 저녁에만 사용하는데 자동문열림 되니 아침되면 건조가 거의 다 되어 있어서 이 기능은 궂이 사용안하게 되네요.가끔 쓸때도 있긴 하겠지만 아주 많진 않을 것 같아요.100도씨 스팀세척 기능은 한번도 안썻어요..사실 열풍건조와 100도씨 스팀세척 기능은 꼭 필요할것 같아서 일부러 이 기능이 있는 제품으로 고른건데, 제 개인적으로는 막상 잘 안쓰게 되는 기능입니다.제품 비교하실 때 각자 환경과 상황 잘 고려하시면 제품선택에 큰 도움이 되지않을까싶습니다.각 기능들은 가벼운 터치로 선택이 가능하구요, 세정코스는 현재 자동에 헹굼1회추가 로 거의 사용하고 있는데요씽큐앱 연동하면 여러 세정코스를 필요시 다운받을 수 있고 상황에 따라 다양하게 사용할 수 있는점은 장점 입니다.내부세척은 월1회정도 하면 되고 씽큐앱 연동해놓으면 내부세척주기 알려줘서 편해요.세척세제도 궂이 살 필요 없이 세제칸에 구연산 넣고 통살균코스(앱에있음) 돌려주면 됩니다.이건 다른 얘기인데요,전에 타사 식세기 사용하다 경험한바. 물병, 식판, 식기류등에 부착하는 네임스티커 또는 제거되지 않은 새제품의 제품스티커는반드시 제거 후 식세기에 넣으세요.자칫 물줄기 나오는 세척날개 내부에 스티커가 들어갈 수 있습니다.어찌 들어가는건지 신기하지만 개인이 못빼고 기사님 모셔야 합니다.설치부터 사용까지 전반적으로 아주 만족하고 있구요약 8년만에 교체한 식세기 인데기술도 많이 발전했고 ㅎㅎ 가전은 역시엘지라는 생각도 듭니다ㅎ식세기 구매를 고려하고 계시다면 저의 리뷰도 조금이나마 도움이되었기를 바랍니다.

Sentence (English): Since I was choosing LG appliances, I chose the Dios without hesitation.
Comments (English): [ Authentic review after using it for about 3 weeks ] || ---------------- || First of all, I'm writing this review with a heavy heart, having experienced a significant price drop about a week after purchase and installation. They say knowledge is medicine, but a first-class refund alone won't be enough to convince you otherwise. Buyers should be especially cautious and thrifty when purchasing expensive appliances. Recently, I moved and needed a dishwasher, so I had it installed. Since I was choosing LG appliances, I chose the Dios without hesitation. The installation was also done by an LG technician. It seats 14 people, so it's ample for a three-person household! It has three tiers, with the lowest tier holding plates, large containers, and a frying pan. Of course, to extend the life of the frying pan, I haven't used the dishwasher. The second tier is for cups, rice bowls, and small plates. The height is adjustable, so it's deep enough to accommodate large bowls. The top tier is for utensils like spoons and ladles. This tier is also height-adjustable, so even large ladles can be easily accommodated. The height adjustment is a huge plus. There are two detergent compartments. Liquid or powder detergent goes in the compartment, and solid detergent goes in the bottom basket, which solves the drawbacks of solid detergents. You can adjust the detergent according to the 15/25 markings on the detergent compartment depending on the amount of dishes you're using. I use Natural Pong liquid detergent, and even though I fill all three compartments, I only use up to the 15 mark. Even with that much, dishes with butter or grease are cleaned thoroughly, and there are almost no water stains even without rinse aid. However, the dishwasher's Tetris performance can affect the quality of the dishwashing, so don't stack the dishes too tightly. The Dios dishwasher has a water softener, but the technician told me that it's not necessary in my area (water softeners vary by area), so I don't use it. This product also has a hot air dryer and a 100°C steam wash. After the initial installation, I used the hot air drying function for a while, but now I don't. (The built-in hot air drying function requires annual air filter replacement.) I use it almost exclusively once a day, in the evening. Since the door automatically opens, the clothes are almost completely dry by morning, so I rarely use this function. I might use it occasionally, but I don't think it'll be very often. I've never used the 100°C steam cleaning function. Honestly, I thought both the hot air drying and 100°C steam cleaning functions were essential, so I deliberately chose a product with these features. Personally, I rarely use them. When comparing products, carefully considering your environment and situation will be a great help. Each function can be selected with a light touch. I currently use the automatic cleaning cycle with an additional rinse. The ThinQ app allows you to download multiple cleaning cycles as needed, allowing you to customize them for different situations. Cleaning the interior is conveniently done about once a month, and if you connect it to the ThinQ app, it will notify you when the internal cleaning cycle is due. You don't even need to buy detergent; just add citric acid to the detergent compartment and run the sterilization cycle (in the app). This is a different story, but based on my experience using a different brand of dishwasher, be sure to remove any name stickers attached to water bottles, plates, cutlery, etc., or any product stickers from new products that haven't been removed before putting them in the dishwasher. Stickers can easily get stuck inside the washing blades where the water sprays out. It's amazing how they get there, but you can't remove them yourself; you'll have to hire a technician. I'm very satisfied with everything from installation to use. I replaced my dishwasher after about eight years, and technology has advanced significantly. LG is the best choice for home appliances. If you're considering purchasing a dishwasher, I hope my review was helpful.

Sentence (English): It seats 14 people, so it's ample for a three-person household!
Comments (English): [ Authentic review after using it for about 3 weeks ] || ---------------- || First of all, I'm writing this review with a heavy heart, having experienced a significant price drop about a week after purchase and installation. They say knowledge is medicine, but a first-class refund alone won't be enough to convince you otherwise. Buyers should be especially cautious and thrifty when purchasing expensive appliances. Recently, I moved and needed a dishwasher, so I had it installed. Since I was choosing LG appliances, I chose the Dios without hesitation. The installation was also done by an LG technician. It seats 14 people, so it's ample for a three-person household! It has three tiers, with the lowest tier holding plates, large containers, and a frying pan. Of course, to extend the life of the frying pan, I haven't used the dishwasher. The second tier is for cups, rice bowls, and small plates. The height is adjustable, so it's deep enough to accommodate large bowls. The top tier is for utensils like spoons and ladles. This tier is also height-adjustable, so even large ladles can be easily accommodated. The height adjustment is a huge plus. There are two detergent compartments. Liquid or powder detergent goes in the compartment, and solid detergent goes in the bottom basket, which solves the drawbacks of solid detergents. You can adjust the detergent according to the 15/25 markings on the detergent compartment depending on the amount of dishes you're using. I use Natural Pong liquid detergent, and even though I fill all three compartments, I only use up to the 15 mark. Even with that much, dishes with butter or grease are cleaned thoroughly, and there are almost no water stains even without rinse aid. However, the dishwasher's Tetris performance can affect the quality of the dishwashing, so don't stack the dishes too tightly. The Dios dishwasher has a water softener, but the technician told me that it's not necessary in my area (water softeners vary by area), so I don't use it. This product also has a hot air dryer and a 100°C steam wash. After the initial installation, I used the hot air drying function for a while, but now I don't. (The built-in hot air drying function requires annual air filter replacement.) I use it almost exclusively once a day, in the evening. Since the door automatically opens, the clothes are almost completely dry by morning, so I rarely use this function. I might use it occasionally, but I don't think it'll be very often. I've never used the 100°C steam cleaning function. Honestly, I thought both the hot air drying and 100°C steam cleaning functions were essential, so I deliberately chose a product with these features. Personally, I rarely use them. When comparing products, carefully considering your environment and situation will be a great help. Each function can be selected with a light touch. I currently use the automatic cleaning cycle with an additional rinse. The ThinQ app allows you to download multiple cleaning cycles as needed, allowing you to customize them for different situations. Cleaning the interior is conveniently done about once a month, and if you connect it to the ThinQ app, it will notify you when the internal cleaning cycle is due. You don't even need to buy detergent; just add citric acid to the detergent compartment and run the sterilization cycle (in the app). This is a different story, but based on my experience using a different brand of dishwasher, be sure to remove any name stickers attached to water bottles, plates, cutlery, etc., or any product stickers from new products that haven't been removed before putting them in the dishwasher. Stickers can easily get stuck inside the washing blades where the water sprays out. It's amazing how they get there, but you can't remove them yourself; you'll have to hire a technician. I'm very satisfied with everything from installation to use. I replaced my dishwasher after about eight years, and technology has advanced significantly. LG is the best choice for home appliances. If you're considering purchasing a dishwasher, I hope my review was helpful.

Comments (English): [ Authentic review after using it for about 3 weeks ] || ---------------- || First of all, I'm writing this review with a heavy heart, having experienced a significant price drop about a week after purchase and installation. They say knowledge is medicine, but a first-class refund alone won't be enough to convince you otherwise. Buyers should be especially cautious and thrifty when purchasing expensive appliances. Recently, I moved and needed a dishwasher, so I had it installed. Since I was choosing LG appliances, I chose the Dios without hesitation. The installation was also done by an LG technician. It seats 14 people, so it's ample for a three-person household! It has three tiers, with the lowest tier holding plates, large containers, and a frying pan. Of course, to extend the life of the frying pan, I haven't used the dishwasher. The second tier is for cups, rice bowls, and small plates. The height is adjustable, so it's deep enough to accommodate large bowls. The top tier is for utensils like spoons and ladles. This tier is also height-adjustable, so even large ladles can be easily accommodated. The height adjustment is a huge plus. There are two detergent compartments. Liquid or powder detergent goes in the compartment, and solid detergent goes in the bottom basket, which solves the drawbacks of solid detergents. You can adjust the detergent according to the 15/25 markings on the detergent compartment depending on the amount of dishes you're using. I use Natural Pong liquid detergent, and even though I fill all three compartments, I only use up to the 15 mark. Even with that much, dishes with butter or grease are cleaned thoroughly, and there are almost no water stains even without rinse aid. However, the dishwasher's Tetris performance can affect the quality of the dishwashing, so don't stack the dishes too tightly. The Dios dishwasher has a water softener, but the technician told me that it's not necessary in my area (water softeners vary by area), so I don't use it. This product also has a hot air dryer and a 100°C steam wash. After the initial installation, I used the hot air drying function for a while, but now I don't. (The built-in hot air drying function requires annual air filter replacement.) I use it almost exclusively once a day, in the evening. Since the door automatically opens, the clothes are almost completely dry by morning, so I rarely use this function. I might use it occasionally, but I don't think it'll be very often. I've never used the 100°C steam cleaning function. Honestly, I thought both the hot air drying and 100°C steam cleaning functions were essential, so I deliberately chose a product with these features. Personally, I rarely use them. When comparing products, carefully considering your environment and situation will be a great help. Each function can be selected with a light touch. I currently use the automatic cleaning cycle with an additional rinse. The ThinQ app allows you to download multiple cleaning cycles as needed, allowing you to customize them for different situations. Cleaning the interior is conveniently done about once a month, and if you connect it to the ThinQ app, it will notify you when the internal cleaning cycle is due. You don't even need to buy detergent; just add citric acid to the detergent compartment and run the sterilization cycle (in the app). This is a different story, but based on my experience using a different brand of dishwasher, be sure to remove any name stickers attached to water bottles, plates, cutlery, etc., or any product stickers from new products that haven't been removed before putting them in the dishwasher. Stickers can easily get stuck inside the washing blades where the water sprays out. It's amazing how they get there, but you can't remove them yourself; you'll have to hire a technician. I'm very satisfied with everything from installation to use. I replaced my dishwasher after about eight years, and technology has advanced significantly. LG is the best choice for home appliances. If you're considering purchasing a dishwasher, I hope my review was helpful.

Comments (English): [ Authentic review after using it for about 3 weeks ] || ---------------- || First of all, I'm writing this review with a heavy heart, having experienced a significant price drop about a week after purchase and installation. They say knowledge is medicine, but a first-class refund alone won't be enough to convince you otherwise. Buyers should be especially cautious and thrifty when purchasing expensive appliances. Recently, I moved and needed a dishwasher, so I had it installed. Since I was choosing LG appliances, I chose the Dios without hesitation. The installation was also done by an LG technician. It seats 14 people, so it's ample for a three-person household! It has three tiers, with the lowest tier holding plates, large containers, and a frying pan. Of course, to extend the life of the frying pan, I haven't used the dishwasher. The second tier is for cups, rice bowls, and small plates. The height is adjustable, so it's deep enough to accommodate large bowls. The top tier is for utensils like spoons and ladles. This tier is also height-adjustable, so even large ladles can be easily accommodated. The height adjustment is a huge plus. There are two detergent compartments. Liquid or powder detergent goes in the compartment, and solid detergent goes in the bottom basket, which solves the drawbacks of solid detergents. You can adjust the detergent according to the 15/25 markings on the detergent compartment depending on the amount of dishes you're using. I use Natural Pong liquid detergent, and even though I fill all three compartments, I only use up to the 15 mark. Even with that much, dishes with butter or grease are cleaned thoroughly, and there are almost no water stains even without rinse aid. However, the dishwasher's Tetris performance can affect the quality of the dishwashing, so don't stack the dishes too tightly. The Dios dishwasher has a water softener, but the technician told me that it's not necessary in my area (water softeners vary by area), so I don't use it. This product also has a hot air dryer and a 100°C steam wash. After the initial installation, I used the hot air drying function for a while, but now I don't. (The built-in hot air drying function requires annual air filter replacement.) I use it almost exclusively once a day, in the evening. Since the door automatically opens, the clothes are almost completely dry by morning, so I rarely use this function. I might use it occasionally, but I don't think it'll be very often. I've never used the 100°C steam cleaning function. Honestly, I thought both the hot air drying and 100°C steam cleaning functions were essential, so I deliberately chose a product with these features. Personally, I rarely use them. When comparing products, carefully considering your environment and situation will be a great help. Each function can be selected with a light touch. I currently use the automatic cleaning cycle with an additional rinse. The ThinQ app allows you to download multiple cleaning cycles as needed, allowing you to customize them for different situations. Cleaning the interior is conveniently done about once a month, and if you connect it to the ThinQ app, it will notify you when the internal cleaning cycle is due. You don't even need to buy detergent; just add citric acid to the detergent compartment and run the sterilization cycle (in the app). This is a different story, but based on my experience using a different brand of dishwasher, be sure to remove any name stickers attached to water bottles, plates, cutlery, etc., or any product stickers from new products that haven't been removed before putting them in the dishwasher. Stickers can easily get stuck inside the washing blades where the water sprays out. It's amazing how they get there, but you can't remove them yourself; you'll have to hire a technician. I'm very satisfied with everything from installation to use. I replaced my dishwasher after about eight years, and technology has advanced significantly. LG is the best choice for home appliances. If you're considering purchasing a dishwasher, I hope my review was helpful.

Comments (English): [ Authentic review after using it for about 3 weeks ] || ---------------- || First of all, I'm writing this review with a heavy heart, having experienced a significant price drop about a week after purchase and installation. They say knowledge is medicine, but a first-class refund alone won't be enough to convince you otherwise. Buyers should be especially cautious and thrifty when purchasing expensive appliances. Recently, I moved and needed a dishwasher, so I had it installed. Since I was choosing LG appliances, I chose the Dios without hesitation. The installation was also done by an LG technician. It seats 14 people, so it's ample for a three-person household! It has three tiers, with the lowest tier holding plates, large containers, and a frying pan. Of course, to extend the life of the frying pan, I haven't used the dishwasher. The second tier is for cups, rice bowls, and small plates. The height is adjustable, so it's deep enough to accommodate large bowls. The top tier is for utensils like spoons and ladles. This tier is also height-adjustable, so even large ladles can be easily accommodated. The height adjustment is a huge plus. There are two detergent compartments. Liquid or powder detergent goes in the compartment, and solid detergent goes in the bottom basket, which solves the drawbacks of solid detergents. You can adjust the detergent according to the 15/25 markings on the detergent compartment depending on the amount of dishes you're using. I use Natural Pong liquid detergent, and even though I fill all three compartments, I only use up to the 15 mark. Even with that much, dishes with butter or grease are cleaned thoroughly, and there are almost no water stains even without rinse aid. However, the dishwasher's Tetris performance can affect the quality of the dishwashing, so don't stack the dishes too tightly. The Dios dishwasher has a water softener, but the technician told me that it's not necessary in my area (water softeners vary by area), so I don't use it. This product also has a hot air dryer and a 100°C steam wash. After the initial installation, I used the hot air drying function for a while, but now I don't. (The built-in hot air drying function requires annual air filter replacement.) I use it almost exclusively once a day, in the evening. Since the door automatically opens, the clothes are almost completely dry by morning, so I rarely use this function. I might use it occasionally, but I don't think it'll be very often. I've never used the 100°C steam cleaning function. Honestly, I thought both the hot air drying and 100°C steam cleaning functions were essential, so I deliberately chose a product with these features. Personally, I rarely use them. When comparing products, carefully considering your environment and situation will be a great help. Each function can be selected with a light touch. I currently use the automatic cleaning cycle with an additional rinse. The ThinQ app allows you to download multiple cleaning cycles as needed, allowing you to customize them for different situations. Cleaning the interior is conveniently done about once a month, and if you connect it to the ThinQ app, it will notify you when the internal cleaning cycle is due. You don't even need to buy detergent; just add citric acid to the detergent compartment and run the sterilization cycle (in the app). This is a different story, but based on my experience using a different brand of dishwasher, be sure to remove any name stickers attached to water bottles, plates, cutlery, etc., or any product stickers from new products that haven't been removed before putting them in the dishwasher. Stickers can easily get stuck inside the washing blades where the water sprays out. It's amazing how they get there, but you can't remove them yourself; you'll have to hire a technician. I'm very satisfied with everything from installation to use. I replaced my dishwasher after about eight years, and technology has advanced significantly. LG is the best choice for home appliances. If you're considering purchasing a dishwasher, I hope my review was helpful.

Sentence (English): The height adjustment is a huge plus.
Comments (English): [ Authentic review after using it for about 3 weeks ] || ---------------- || First of all, I'm writing this review with a heavy heart, having experienced a significant price drop about a week after purchase and installation. They say knowledge is medicine, but a first-class refund alone won't be enough to convince you otherwise. Buyers should be especially cautious and thrifty when purchasing expensive appliances. Recently, I moved and needed a dishwasher, so I had it installed. Since I was choosing LG appliances, I chose the Dios without hesitation. The installation was also done by an LG technician. It seats 14 people, so it's ample for a three-person household! It has three tiers, with the lowest tier holding plates, large containers, and a frying pan. Of course, to extend the life of the frying pan, I haven't used the dishwasher. The second tier is for cups, rice bowls, and small plates. The height is adjustable, so it's deep enough to accommodate large bowls. The top tier is for utensils like spoons and ladles. This tier is also height-adjustable, so even large ladles can be easily accommodated. The height adjustment is a huge plus. There are two detergent compartments. Liquid or powder detergent goes in the compartment, and solid detergent goes in the bottom basket, which solves the drawbacks of solid detergents. You can adjust the detergent according to the 15/25 markings on the detergent compartment depending on the amount of dishes you're using. I use Natural Pong liquid detergent, and even though I fill all three compartments, I only use up to the 15 mark. Even with that much, dishes with butter or grease are cleaned thoroughly, and there are almost no water stains even without rinse aid. However, the dishwasher's Tetris performance can affect the quality of the dishwashing, so don't stack the dishes too tightly. The Dios dishwasher has a water softener, but the technician told me that it's not necessary in my area (water softeners vary by area), so I don't use it. This product also has a hot air dryer and a 100°C steam wash. After the initial installation, I used the hot air drying function for a while, but now I don't. (The built-in hot air drying function requires annual air filter replacement.) I use it almost exclusively once a day, in the evening. Since the door automatically opens, the clothes are almost completely dry by morning, so I rarely use this function. I might use it occasionally, but I don't think it'll be very often. I've never used the 100°C steam cleaning function. Honestly, I thought both the hot air drying and 100°C steam cleaning functions were essential, so I deliberately chose a product with these features. Personally, I rarely use them. When comparing products, carefully considering your environment and situation will be a great help. Each function can be selected with a light touch. I currently use the automatic cleaning cycle with an additional rinse. The ThinQ app allows you to download multiple cleaning cycles as needed, allowing you to customize them for different situations. Cleaning the interior is conveniently done about once a month, and if you connect it to the ThinQ app, it will notify you when the internal cleaning cycle is due. You don't even need to buy detergent; just add citric acid to the detergent compartment and run the sterilization cycle (in the app). This is a different story, but based on my experience using a different brand of dishwasher, be sure to remove any name stickers attached to water bottles, plates, cutlery, etc., or any product stickers from new products that haven't been removed before putting them in the dishwasher. Stickers can easily get stuck inside the washing blades where the water sprays out. It's amazing how they get there, but you can't remove them yourself; you'll have to hire a technician. I'm very satisfied with everything from installation to use. I replaced my dishwasher after about eight years, and technology has advanced significantly. LG is the best choice for home appliances. If you're considering purchasing a dishwasher, I hope my review was helpful.

Comments (English): [ Authentic review after using it for about 3 weeks ] || ---------------- || First of all, I'm writing this review with a heavy heart, having experienced a significant price drop about a week after purchase and installation. They say knowledge is medicine, but a first-class refund alone won't be enough to convince you otherwise. Buyers should be especially cautious and thrifty when purchasing expensive appliances. Recently, I moved and needed a dishwasher, so I had it installed. Since I was choosing LG appliances, I chose the Dios without hesitation. The installation was also done by an LG technician. It seats 14 people, so it's ample for a three-person household! It has three tiers, with the lowest tier holding plates, large containers, and a frying pan. Of course, to extend the life of the frying pan, I haven't used the dishwasher. The second tier is for cups, rice bowls, and small plates. The height is adjustable, so it's deep enough to accommodate large bowls. The top tier is for utensils like spoons and ladles. This tier is also height-adjustable, so even large ladles can be easily accommodated. The height adjustment is a huge plus. There are two detergent compartments. Liquid or powder detergent goes in the compartment, and solid detergent goes in the bottom basket, which solves the drawbacks of solid detergents. You can adjust the detergent according to the 15/25 markings on the detergent compartment depending on the amount of dishes you're using. I use Natural Pong liquid detergent, and even though I fill all three compartments, I only use up to the 15 mark. Even with that much, dishes with butter or grease are cleaned thoroughly, and there are almost no water stains even without rinse aid. However, the dishwasher's Tetris performance can affect the quality of the dishwashing, so don't stack the dishes too tightly. The Dios dishwasher has a water softener, but the technician told me that it's not necessary in my area (water softeners vary by area), so I don't use it. This product also has a hot air dryer and a 100°C steam wash. After the initial installation, I used the hot air drying function for a while, but now I don't. (The built-in hot air drying function requires annual air filter replacement.) I use it almost exclusively once a day, in the evening. Since the door automatically opens, the clothes are almost completely dry by morning, so I rarely use this function. I might use it occasionally, but I don't think it'll be very often. I've never used the 100°C steam cleaning function. Honestly, I thought both the hot air drying and 100°C steam cleaning functions were essential, so I deliberately chose a product with these features. Personally, I rarely use them. When comparing products, carefully considering your environment and situation will be a great help. Each function can be selected with a light touch. I currently use the automatic cleaning cycle with an additional rinse. The ThinQ app allows you to download multiple cleaning cycles as needed, allowing you to customize them for different situations. Cleaning the interior is conveniently done about once a month, and if you connect it to the ThinQ app, it will notify you when the internal cleaning cycle is due. You don't even need to buy detergent; just add citric acid to the detergent compartment and run the sterilization cycle (in the app). This is a different story, but based on my experience using a different brand of dishwasher, be sure to remove any name stickers attached to water bottles, plates, cutlery, etc., or any product stickers from new products that haven't been removed before putting them in the dishwasher. Stickers can easily get stuck inside the washing blades where the water sprays out. It's amazing how they get there, but you can't remove them yourself; you'll have to hire a technician. I'm very satisfied with everything from installation to use. I replaced my dishwasher after about eight years, and technology has advanced significantly. LG is the best choice for home appliances. If you're considering purchasing a dishwasher, I hope my review was helpful.

Sentence (English): I use Natural Pong liquid detergent, and even though I fill all three compartments, I only use up to the 15 mark.
Comments (English): [ Authentic review after using it for about 3 weeks ] || ---------------- || First of all, I'm writing this review with a heavy heart, having experienced a significant price drop about a week after purchase and installation. They say knowledge is medicine, but a first-class refund alone won't be enough to convince you otherwise. Buyers should be especially cautious and thrifty when purchasing expensive appliances. Recently, I moved and needed a dishwasher, so I had it installed. Since I was choosing LG appliances, I chose the Dios without hesitation. The installation was also done by an LG technician. It seats 14 people, so it's ample for a three-person household! It has three tiers, with the lowest tier holding plates, large containers, and a frying pan. Of course, to extend the life of the frying pan, I haven't used the dishwasher. The second tier is for cups, rice bowls, and small plates. The height is adjustable, so it's deep enough to accommodate large bowls. The top tier is for utensils like spoons and ladles. This tier is also height-adjustable, so even large ladles can be easily accommodated. The height adjustment is a huge plus. There are two detergent compartments. Liquid or powder detergent goes in the compartment, and solid detergent goes in the bottom basket, which solves the drawbacks of solid detergents. You can adjust the detergent according to the 15/25 markings on the detergent compartment depending on the amount of dishes you're using. I use Natural Pong liquid detergent, and even though I fill all three compartments, I only use up to the 15 mark. Even with that much, dishes with butter or grease are cleaned thoroughly, and there are almost no water stains even without rinse aid. However, the dishwasher's Tetris performance can affect the quality of the dishwashing, so don't stack the dishes too tightly. The Dios dishwasher has a water softener, but the technician told me that it's not necessary in my area (water softeners vary by area), so I don't use it. This product also has a hot air dryer and a 100°C steam wash. After the initial installation, I used the hot air drying function for a while, but now I don't. (The built-in hot air drying function requires annual air filter replacement.) I use it almost exclusively once a day, in the evening. Since the door automatically opens, the clothes are almost completely dry by morning, so I rarely use this function. I might use it occasionally, but I don't think it'll be very often. I've never used the 100°C steam cleaning function. Honestly, I thought both the hot air drying and 100°C steam cleaning functions were essential, so I deliberately chose a product with these features. Personally, I rarely use them. When comparing products, carefully considering your environment and situation will be a great help. Each function can be selected with a light touch. I currently use the automatic cleaning cycle with an additional rinse. The ThinQ app allows you to download multiple cleaning cycles as needed, allowing you to customize them for different situations. Cleaning the interior is conveniently done about once a month, and if you connect it to the ThinQ app, it will notify you when the internal cleaning cycle is due. You don't even need to buy detergent; just add citric acid to the detergent compartment and run the sterilization cycle (in the app). This is a different story, but based on my experience using a different brand of dishwasher, be sure to remove any name stickers attached to water bottles, plates, cutlery, etc., or any product stickers from new products that haven't been removed before putting them in the dishwasher. Stickers can easily get stuck inside the washing blades where the water sprays out. It's amazing how they get there, but you can't remove them yourself; you'll have to hire a technician. I'm very satisfied with everything from installation to use. I replaced my dishwasher after about eight years, and technology has advanced significantly. LG is the best choice for home appliances. If you're considering purchasing a dishwasher, I hope my review was helpful.

Comments (English): [ Authentic review after using it for about 3 weeks ] || ---------------- || First of all, I'm writing this review with a heavy heart, having experienced a significant price drop about a week after purchase and installation. They say knowledge is medicine, but a first-class refund alone won't be enough to convince you otherwise. Buyers should be especially cautious and thrifty when purchasing expensive appliances. Recently, I moved and needed a dishwasher, so I had it installed. Since I was choosing LG appliances, I chose the Dios without hesitation. The installation was also done by an LG technician. It seats 14 people, so it's ample for a three-person household! It has three tiers, with the lowest tier holding plates, large containers, and a frying pan. Of course, to extend the life of the frying pan, I haven't used the dishwasher. The second tier is for cups, rice bowls, and small plates. The height is adjustable, so it's deep enough to accommodate large bowls. The top tier is for utensils like spoons and ladles. This tier is also height-adjustable, so even large ladles can be easily accommodated. The height adjustment is a huge plus. There are two detergent compartments. Liquid or powder detergent goes in the compartment, and solid detergent goes in the bottom basket, which solves the drawbacks of solid detergents. You can adjust the detergent according to the 15/25 markings on the detergent compartment depending on the amount of dishes you're using. I use Natural Pong liquid detergent, and even though I fill all three compartments, I only use up to the 15 mark. Even with that much, dishes with butter or grease are cleaned thoroughly, and there are almost no water stains even without rinse aid. However, the dishwasher's Tetris performance can affect the quality of the dishwashing, so don't stack the dishes too tightly. The Dios dishwasher has a water softener, but the technician told me that it's not necessary in my area (water softeners vary by area), so I don't use it. This product also has a hot air dryer and a 100°C steam wash. After the initial installation, I used the hot air drying function for a while, but now I don't. (The built-in hot air drying function requires annual air filter replacement.) I use it almost exclusively once a day, in the evening. Since the door automatically opens, the clothes are almost completely dry by morning, so I rarely use this function. I might use it occasionally, but I don't think it'll be very often. I've never used the 100°C steam cleaning function. Honestly, I thought both the hot air drying and 100°C steam cleaning functions were essential, so I deliberately chose a product with these features. Personally, I rarely use them. When comparing products, carefully considering your environment and situation will be a great help. Each function can be selected with a light touch. I currently use the automatic cleaning cycle with an additional rinse. The ThinQ app allows you to download multiple cleaning cycles as needed, allowing you to customize them for different situations. Cleaning the interior is conveniently done about once a month, and if you connect it to the ThinQ app, it will notify you when the internal cleaning cycle is due. You don't even need to buy detergent; just add citric acid to the detergent compartment and run the sterilization cycle (in the app). This is a different story, but based on my experience using a different brand of dishwasher, be sure to remove any name stickers attached to water bottles, plates, cutlery, etc., or any product stickers from new products that haven't been removed before putting them in the dishwasher. Stickers can easily get stuck inside the washing blades where the water sprays out. It's amazing how they get there, but you can't remove them yourself; you'll have to hire a technician. I'm very satisfied with everything from installation to use. I replaced my dishwasher after about eight years, and technology has advanced significantly. LG is the best choice for home appliances. If you're considering purchasing a dishwasher, I hope my review was helpful.

Sentence (English): The Dios dishwasher has a water softener, but the technician told me that it's not necessary in my area (water softeners vary by area), so I don't use it.
Comments (English): [ Authentic review after using it for about 3 weeks ] || ---------------- || First of all, I'm writing this review with a heavy heart, having experienced a significant price drop about a week after purchase and installation. They say knowledge is medicine, but a first-class refund alone won't be enough to convince you otherwise. Buyers should be especially cautious and thrifty when purchasing expensive appliances. Recently, I moved and needed a dishwasher, so I had it installed. Since I was choosing LG appliances, I chose the Dios without hesitation. The installation was also done by an LG technician. It seats 14 people, so it's ample for a three-person household! It has three tiers, with the lowest tier holding plates, large containers, and a frying pan. Of course, to extend the life of the frying pan, I haven't used the dishwasher. The second tier is for cups, rice bowls, and small plates. The height is adjustable, so it's deep enough to accommodate large bowls. The top tier is for utensils like spoons and ladles. This tier is also height-adjustable, so even large ladles can be easily accommodated. The height adjustment is a huge plus. There are two detergent compartments. Liquid or powder detergent goes in the compartment, and solid detergent goes in the bottom basket, which solves the drawbacks of solid detergents. You can adjust the detergent according to the 15/25 markings on the detergent compartment depending on the amount of dishes you're using. I use Natural Pong liquid detergent, and even though I fill all three compartments, I only use up to the 15 mark. Even with that much, dishes with butter or grease are cleaned thoroughly, and there are almost no water stains even without rinse aid. However, the dishwasher's Tetris performance can affect the quality of the dishwashing, so don't stack the dishes too tightly. The Dios dishwasher has a water softener, but the technician told me that it's not necessary in my area (water softeners vary by area), so I don't use it. This product also has a hot air dryer and a 100°C steam wash. After the initial installation, I used the hot air drying function for a while, but now I don't. (The built-in hot air drying function requires annual air filter replacement.) I use it almost exclusively once a day, in the evening. Since the door automatically opens, the clothes are almost completely dry by morning, so I rarely use this function. I might use it occasionally, but I don't think it'll be very often. I've never used the 100°C steam cleaning function. Honestly, I thought both the hot air drying and 100°C steam cleaning functions were essential, so I deliberately chose a product with these features. Personally, I rarely use them. When comparing products, carefully considering your environment and situation will be a great help. Each function can be selected with a light touch. I currently use the automatic cleaning cycle with an additional rinse. The ThinQ app allows you to download multiple cleaning cycles as needed, allowing you to customize them for different situations. Cleaning the interior is conveniently done about once a month, and if you connect it to the ThinQ app, it will notify you when the internal cleaning cycle is due. You don't even need to buy detergent; just add citric acid to the detergent compartment and run the sterilization cycle (in the app). This is a different story, but based on my experience using a different brand of dishwasher, be sure to remove any name stickers attached to water bottles, plates, cutlery, etc., or any product stickers from new products that haven't been removed before putting them in the dishwasher. Stickers can easily get stuck inside the washing blades where the water sprays out. It's amazing how they get there, but you can't remove them yourself; you'll have to hire a technician. I'm very satisfied with everything from installation to use. I replaced my dishwasher after about eight years, and technology has advanced significantly. LG is the best choice for home appliances. If you're considering purchasing a dishwasher, I hope my review was helpful.
